subject: Day 1: Two ways to live
title: Two ways to live
body:
Good morning.

Psalm 1 opens the whole book with a choice: a tree planted by streams, or chaff the wind blows away. Rooted people are thankful people, because they know where their water comes from.
prompt: Thank God for two places He has rooted you: a person and a place.

subject: Day 2: What is man?
title: What is man?
body:
Good morning.

David looks up at the night sky and cannot believe God bothers with us. He made the moon and the stars, and He is mindful of you.
prompt: Step outside or look out a window. Thank Him for three things He made.

subject: Day 3: Honest and hopeful
title: Honest and hopeful
body:
Good morning.

Psalm 13 starts with How long, O Lord? and ends with singing. Gratitude does not mean pretending. It means finishing the sentence the way David does: But I trust in your unfailing love.
prompt: Thank God for one hard season He carried you through.

subject: Day 4: A good inheritance
title: A good inheritance
body:
Good morning.

The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places. David is thankful for the life he actually has, not the one he might have had.
prompt: Name three ordinary things about your life you would miss terribly.

subject: Day 5: The Shepherd
title: The Shepherd
body:
Good morning.

You know this one by heart. Read it slowly anyway. Every line is something to be thankful for: rest, guidance, presence in the valley, a table, a cup running over.
prompt: Pick three gifts straight out of Psalm 23 and thank Him for your version of them.

subject: Day 6: Joy in the morning
title: Joy in the morning
body:
Good morning.

Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning. David wrote this at a dedication, looking back at what God brought him through.
prompt: Thank God for a morning that came after a long night.

subject: Day 7: Taste and see
title: Taste and see
body:
Good morning.

I sought the Lord, and he answered me and delivered me from all my fears. Psalm 34 invites you to test the goodness of God like you would taste a meal.
prompt: Thank Him for a prayer He answered, even one you had forgotten you prayed.

subject: Day 8: Out of the pit
title: Out of the pit
body:
Good morning.

He lifted me out of the slimy pit and set my feet on a rock and put a new song in my mouth. That is a testimony in one verse.
prompt: Thank God for where you are not anymore.

subject: Day 9: Thirsty
title: Thirsty
body:
Good morning.

As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul pants for you. Even the wanting is a gift, because it means there is a stream.
prompt: Thank God for the hunger itself, that you want more of Him at all.

subject: Day 10: A very present help
title: A very present help
body:
Good morning.

God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear, though the earth give way. Therefore is the thankful word in that verse.
prompt: Thank Him for the trouble that did not swallow you.

subject: Day 11: A clean heart
title: A clean heart
body:
Good morning.

Psalm 51 is David at his worst, asking for mercy. The most thankful people are forgiven people who know it.
prompt: Thank God for one specific thing He has forgiven you for.

subject: Day 12: Under His wings
title: Under His wings
body:
Good morning.

David wrote this hiding in a cave, and still says: I will take refuge in the shadow of your wings until the disaster has passed. Gratitude can live in a cave.
prompt: Thank Him for the shelter you are under right now: home, church, friendship.

subject: Day 13: The overflowing cart
title: The overflowing cart
body:
Good morning.

You crown the year with your bounty, and your carts overflow with abundance. Psalm 65 is the harvest psalm, and November is the harvest month.
prompt: Thank God for three things on your table this week.

subject: Day 14: Come and hear
title: Come and hear
body:
Good morning.

Come and hear, all you who fear God; let me tell you what he has done for me. Gratitude is meant to be said out loud to somebody.
prompt: Tell one person today something God has done for you. Then write it down.

subject: Day 15: Nothing on earth
title: Nothing on earth
body:
Good morning.

Whom have I in heaven but you? And earth has nothing I desire besides you. Asaph almost lost his footing envying others, until he got honest about what he actually had.
prompt: Thank God for something money did not buy.

subject: Day 16: Remember the deeds
title: Remember the deeds
body:
Good morning.

I will remember the deeds of the Lord. When Asaph could not feel God in the present, he thanked Him for the past, and it steadied him.
prompt: Write down three things God did for you in years past.

subject: Day 17: Better is one day
title: Better is one day
body:
Good morning.

Better is one day in your courts than a thousand elsewhere. The sparrow found a home near the altar. So did you.
prompt: Thank God for your church, or the people who are church to you.

subject: Day 18: Teach us to number
title: Teach us to number
body:
Good morning.

Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom. Moses wrote this one. Counting days and counting blessings turn out to be the same skill.
prompt: Thank God for your age, exactly the number it is, and one gift that came with it.

subject: Day 19: Under His feathers
title: Under His feathers
body:
Good morning.

He will cover you with his feathers, and under his wings you will find refuge. Someone you love has been kept safe more times than you know.
prompt: Thank God for protection you never saw, the near misses you slept through.

subject: Day 20: Enter with thanksgiving
title: Enter with thanksgiving
body:
Good morning.

Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise. Psalm 100 is five verses long. Read it twice, once quietly and once out loud.
prompt: Thank Him today for who He is, not what He gives. Three things about Him.

subject: Day 21: Forget not
title: Forget not
body:
Good morning.

Praise the Lord, my soul, and forget not all his benefits. Then David lists them: forgiveness, healing, redemption, love, renewal. This psalm is a gratitude list with a melody.
prompt: Borrow David's list. Which three of his benefits are yours today?

subject: Day 22: Let the redeemed say so
title: Let the redeemed say so
body:
Good morning.

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good. Four times in this psalm, people in trouble cry out, He delivers them, and then: let them give thanks. That is the pattern of a whole life.
prompt: Say so. Thank God in writing for the deliverance story only you can tell.

subject: Day 23: From the rising of the sun
title: From the rising of the sun
body:
Good morning.

From the rising of the sun to the place where it sets, the name of the Lord is to be praised. He raises the poor from the dust. God stoops low, and that is worth everything.
prompt: Thank God for a time He met you when you were low.

subject: Day 24: This is the day
title: This is the day
body:
Good morning.

This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it. Psalm 118 was likely the hymn Jesus sang on the night He was betrayed. He gave thanks that night too.
prompt: Thank God for today. Not a better day, this one. Three reasons.

subject: Day 25: He watches over you
title: He watches over you
body:
Good morning.

He who watches over you will not slumber. Every trip you took this year, every night you slept, He was awake.
prompt: Thank God for safe travels and quiet nights, this week and this year.

subject: Day 26: Filled with laughter
title: Filled with laughter
body:
Good morning.

Our mouths were filled with laughter, our tongues with songs of joy. The Lord has done great things for us. Happy Thanksgiving. This psalm was written for a day exactly like today.
prompt: At the table today, let everyone answer: what great thing has He done for us this year?

subject: Day 27: Servants by night
title: Servants by night
body:
Good morning.

Psalm 134 is three verses, sung by those keeping watch in the temple at night. Even the night shift blesses the Lord.
prompt: Thank God for the people who serve while you sleep, and name a few.

subject: Day 28: His love endures forever
title: His love endures forever
body:
Good morning.

Twenty-six verses, and every one ends the same way: His love endures forever. Creation, rescue, provision, all of it hangs on that one refrain.
prompt: Write your own three verses. Three moments from your life, each ending: His love endures forever.

subject: Day 29: One generation to another
title: One generation to another
body:
Good morning.

One generation commends your works to another. Someone told you about God. Someone will hear it from you.
prompt: Thank God for the person who first told you about Him, by name.

subject: Day 30: Let everything that has breath
title: Let everything that has breath
body:
Good morning.

The book ends with nothing but praise. No requests, no complaints, just six verses of hallelujah. You have breath. That is the last reason on the list, and the first.
prompt: Read back through your whole month of thanks. Then add the final three.
